title: Create an Error Boundary & Custom 404
description: Add an error boundary to a product page that catches rendering errors, and build a custom 404 page.
problemStatement:
## Goal You will implement robust error handling: a segment‑level error boundary for a products page and a custom Not Found page for unmatched routes. ### Requirements 1. **Custom 404 (App Router):** - Create `app/not-found.js`. - It should display an `

404 – Oops!

` and a link back to the homepage using `next/link`. 2. **Error Boundary:** - Create a products page at `app/products/page.js` that imports a `ProductList` Server Component (which might throw). - Create `app/products/error.js` (Client Component) that shows the error message and a "Try again" button calling `reset()`. 3. **Simulate an Error:** - In `ProductList.js`, add a button that causes a render error when clicked (e.g., throw an error inside a conditional). Use `'use client'` for that part, but the main list can remain server‑rendered. - Ensure the error boundary catches the error and displays the fallback. 4. **Verify:** - Visit `/nonexistent` → see the custom 404. - Visit `/products`, click the error trigger → see the error fallback, click Try again → return to the product list. ### Note For the error simulation, you can wrap a part of the page in a client component that calls `throw new Error('Test crash')` on a button click. That error will be caught by the nearest error boundary.
hints: `error.js` must have `'use client'` because it uses interactive button and `reset()`.
Use `notFound()` from `next/navigation` if you want to trigger 404 programmatically, but for this task just use `not-found.js`.
The error boundary only catches rendering errors, so your error must be thrown during render, not in an event handler. Use `useState` to trigger a re‑render that throws.
expectedOutput: Custom 404 page shown for unknown routes. Error boundary catches the test error on the products page and allows recovery.
